examples.why: hex-כבד is a clumsy half-translated hybrid (keep heavy-hex or use משושה כבד); החומרה המטרה is a calque of "target hardware"; כל אורביטל 4 is ungrammatical for "every 4th orbital" — only the (0, 4, 8) list makes it parseable.

examples.source: Since our molecule has a closed-shell Hartree-Fock state ... We will use a fake 127-qubit backend
examples.suggested: מכיוון שלמולקולה שלנו יש מצב Hartree-Fock עם קליפה סגורה ... נשתמש ב-Backend מדומה בן 127 קיוביטים
examples.translation: מכיוון שמולקולתנו בעלת מצב Hartree-Fock עם קליפה סגורה ... נשתמש ב-Backend מדומה בת 127 qubit
examples.why: מולקולתנו is a literary possessive suffix out of step with the file's otherwise informal register; בת 127 is a gender mismatch with Backend, and the surrounding text elsewhere writes "36 qubit" / "qubit פיזיים" with an English singular where Hebrew needs a plural.

examples.source: Probabilistically create batches of subsamples from recovered bitstrings.
examples.suggested: יצירה הסתברותית של אצוות של תת-דגימות מהמחרוזות המשוחזרות.
examples.translation: יצירה הסתברותית של אצוות משניות מהמחרוזות המשוחזרות.
examples.why: "batches of subsamples" became "secondary/sub-batches" — the subsample level of the SQD loop is flattened out of the step list, though the code and the callback output ("Subsample 0") restore it.

editor_note: No semantic drift: every quantity, threshold and caveat survives intact (7 slices / 6 of 8 allotted groups, "grows past 8" → "יעלה על 8", "8 or fewer" → "ב-8 ... או פחות", 5e-3 × 10 = 5e-2, the 1e-4 tolerance note), and the core conventions are correct and consistent — "הפצה לאחור" for backpropagation, "פרוסות" for slices, "מתחלפות" for commuting, "המילטוניאן", observable/backend/transpile kept in English. What a native technical editor would still change is surface polish. The passive of לקצץ is written as the non-existent form "שנוקצצו" (should be "שקוצצו"); several calqued constructions read as translation, not Hebrew writing — "משמע זאת ש" for "this implies that", "כעת שיש לנו" for "now that we have", "גודל ה-observable הפלט" for "the size of the output observable" (two definites in apposition), and "מדריך כיצד לעשות" for "how-to guide" (in one place split as "ראה ב[מדריך כיצד לעשות] זה"). Terminology nits: "qubit operator" flattens to "האופרטור הקוונטי" (quantum operator), the term is introduced once as "אובייקט Observable של פאולי" but is plain "ה-observable" everywhere after, and "Qubits/qubits" alternates in casing across the file.

examples.source: ...proportional to the magnitude of the truncated terms' coefficients.
examples.suggested: ...שהיא פרופורציונלית לגודל המקדמים של האיברים שקוצצו.
examples.translation: ...שהיא פרופורציונלית לגודל המקדמים של האיברים שנוקצצו.
examples.why: "שנוקצצו" is not a real Hebrew verb form — the passive of the pi'el לקצץ is pu'al קוצצו. A native writer would never produce this hybrid nif'al/pu'al form.

examples.source: From the qubit operator, we can generate a quantum circuit which models its time evolution.
examples.suggested: מאופרטור הקיוביטים, אנחנו יכולים לייצר מעגל קוונטי שמדמה את אבולוציית הזמן שלו.
examples.translation: מהאופרטור הקוונטי, אנחנו יכולים לייצר מעגל קוונטי שמדמה את אבולוציית הזמן שלו.
examples.why: "qubit operator" is a specific term (the Pauli operator on the qubit register); rendering it "אופרטור קוונטי" (quantum operator) drops the qubit qualifier and generalizes the term. Recognizable, not misleading, but imprecise.

examples.source: This implies that backpropagating one more slice would cause the number of Pauli groups to exceed 8.
examples.suggested: משמעות הדבר היא שהפצה לאחור של פרוסה נוספת תגרום למספר קבוצות הפאולי לחרוג מ-8.
examples.translation: משמע זאת שהפצה לאחור של פרוסה נוספת תגרום למספר קבוצות הפאולי לחרוג מ-8.
examples.why: "משמע זאת ש" is an inverted, non-idiomatic construction; Hebrew takes "משמעות הדבר היא ש" or "זאת אומרת ש". Reads as word-order transfer from English.

examples.source: Next, we will specify the same problem with the same constraints on the size of the output observable.
examples.suggested: ...עם אותן מגבלות על גודל ה-observable שבפלט.
examples.translation: לאחר מכן, נציין את אותה הבעיה עם אותן מגבלות על גודל ה-observable הפלט.
examples.why: "ה-observable הפלט" stacks two definite nouns in apposition — a direct calque of the English noun-noun compound that is ungrammatical in Hebrew.

examples.source: Now that we have our reduced ansatze and expanded observables, we can transpile our experiments to the backend.
examples.suggested: כעת, כשיש לנו את ה-ansatze המצומצמים וה-observables המורחבים, נוכל לבצע Transpile לניסויים שלנו עבור ה-Backend.
examples.translation: כעת שיש לנו את ה-ansatze המצומצמים וה-observables המורחבים, נוכל לבצע Transpile לניסויים שלנו עבור ה-Backend.
examples.why: "כעת ש..." is a literal mapping of "now that"; Hebrew requires "כעת, כש..." / "עכשיו כש...". Grammatical-sounding to an MT checker, jarring to a native reader.

examples.source: Backpropagate slices from the circuit onto a Pauli observable
examples.suggested: הפצה לאחור של פרוסות מהמעגל אל observable של פאולי
examples.translation: הפצה לאחור של פרוסות מהמעגל אל אובייקט Observable של פאולי
examples.why: Adds "אובייקט" (object), which the English does not say and which mis-frames the observable as a programming object; it also capitalizes Observable here while every later mention is plain "ה-observable". Same casing drift affects Qubits/qubits across the file.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no dropped caveats, numbers (56 qubit, empat langkah waktu, dua bit, interval 30 hari, 1 Nov 2022–1 Apr 2023) and the QUBO objective list all match the English, and the informal "kamu/-mu" convention holds. What a native editor would change is terminology consistency: "circuit" appears as capitalized English "Circuit kuantum" (lines 39, 218, 227) alongside Indonesian "sirkuit" (216, "optimasi sirkuit" in 218), and "backend" likewise as capitalized "Backend `ibm_torino`" (50) vs lowercase "backend kuantum" (227) — these read as glossary-substitution artifacts, not authorial choices. "Risk aversion" is rendered twice differently ("koefisien penghindaran risiko" line 37 vs untranslated "koefisien risk aversion" line 179), as is "hardware-efficient" ("efisien secara perangkat keras" line 48, a calque, vs the better "hemat perangkat keras" line 218); "manuskrip kami" (37) also becomes "paper kami" (179). Finally the first-person plural splits mid-document — "kami" in Background/Step 1, "kita" from Step 2 onward — and line 314 is visibly calqued ("untuk perbandingan lebih mudah tentang bagaimana proses optimasi berbeda dari sampling acak dalam hal biaya"). None of this misleads a learner.

examples.source: the quantum circuit estimates the cost function … configures the quantum circuit ansatz … The total number of circuits
examples.suggested: sirkuit kuantum memperkirakan fungsi biaya … mengonfigurasi ansatz sirkuit kuantum
examples.translation: Circuit kuantum memperkirakan fungsi biaya … mengonfigurasi ansatz Circuit kuantum … Jumlah total sirkuit
examples.why: Same term rendered two ways in the same file: capitalized English "Circuit" (3x) vs Indonesian "sirkuit" (2x, including "optimasi sirkuit" in the very same sentence as "ansatz Circuit kuantum"). The capitalized mid-sentence English reads as a glossary-substitution artifact rather than a deliberate keep-in-English choice; the same happens with "Backend `ibm_torino`" (line 50) against "backend kuantum" (line 227).

examples.source: where $\gamma$ is the risk aversion coefficient … we set the maximum investment per asset, the risk aversion coefficient
examples.suggested: … koefisien penghindaran risiko (risk aversion)
examples.translation: di mana $\gamma$ adalah koefisien penghindaran risiko … kita mengatur investasi maksimum per aset, koefisien risk aversion
examples.why: The same parameter is named in Indonesian in Background and left in raw English in Step 2, so a reader may not connect the `risk_aversion` setting with the $\gamma$ defined earlier. Same split affects "manuskrip kami" (37) vs "paper kami" (179).

examples.source: a customized and hardware-efficient adaptation of the standard Real Amplitudes ansatz … which is a hardware-efficient ansatz designed for financial optimization problems
examples.suggested: adaptasi … yang hemat perangkat keras (hardware-efficient) dari ansatz Real Amplitudes standar
examples.translation: sebuah adaptasi yang disesuaikan dan efisien secara perangkat keras dari ansatz Real Amplitudes standar … yaitu ansatz yang hemat perangkat keras
examples.why: "efisien secara perangkat keras" is a word-for-word calque of the English compound and is not how an Indonesian author would phrase it; the file itself uses the better "hemat perangkat keras" twenty lines later, so the term is both calqued and inconsistent.

examples.source: We plot both distributions normalized in amplitude for easier comparison of how the optimization process differs from random sampling in terms of cost.
examples.suggested: Kedua distribusi kami plot dengan amplitudo ternormalisasi agar lebih mudah membandingkan perbedaan biaya antara proses optimasi dan sampling acak.
examples.translation: Kita memplot kedua distribusi yang dinormalisasi dalam amplitudo untuk perbandingan lebih mudah tentang bagaimana proses optimasi berbeda dari sampling acak dalam hal biaya.
examples.why: "untuk perbandingan lebih mudah tentang bagaimana …" mirrors the English nominal phrase "for easier comparison of how …", a construction Indonesian technical prose does not use; a native writer would turn it into a verbal clause ("agar lebih mudah membandingkan …").

examples.source: We solve using a hybrid quantum-classical method … We define the number of time steps … we execute the optimization
examples.suggested: Pick one — "kita" throughout (inclusive, matches the tutorial's teaching voice) or "kami" throughout.
examples.translation: Kami menyelesaikannya menggunakan metode hibrida … Kita menentukan jumlah langkah waktu … kita menjalankan optimasi
examples.why: The authorial "we" switches from exclusive "kami" (Background through Step 1) to inclusive "kita" (Step 2 onward) with no change in the English, so the narrative voice shifts mid-tutorial: "kami" excludes the reader while "kita" includes them.

editor_note: Nothing here misleads a learner — the physics prose is accurate ("Bell state (dua qubit yang saling terjerat)", "pembagian yang hampir merata antara '00' dan '11'", "Pengukuran seharusnya berubah menjadi 000 dan 111"), and the keep-in-English convention for qubit/gate/circuit/Bell state/shots is the right call for Indonesian. But a native technical editor would fix four things. (1) The "under" qualifier is dropped twice — both the frontmatter description and the intro render "in under two minutes" as plain "dalam dua menit", turning a ceiling into a flat duration. (2) Second-person address is mixed inside single sentences: "jadi Anda bisa menginstal paket apa pun ... tanpa memengaruhi lingkungan Python 'dasar' di mesinmu" and "jika lingkungan Python-mu rusak, Anda bisa dengan mudah menghapusnya" swap between formal "Anda" and clitic "-mu" mid-clause. (3) Entanglement is split within the file between the Indonesian "saling terjerat" (sections 2 and 4) and the untouched English "quantum entanglement" (section 3) — recognizable, but inconsistent. (4) Residual translationese/casing: "navigasi ke direktori proyekmu" is a calque of "navigate to", "Tapi Anda bisa juga" is colloquial where "Namun" belongs, and "Circuit" is left title-cased mid-sentence ("di akhir Circuit", "menjalankan Circuit di hardware quantum nyata") as heading capitalization bleeding into body text.

examples.source: Build and visualize a quantum circuit in under two minutes / Build your first quantum circuit in under two minutes
examples.suggested: dalam waktu kurang dari dua menit
examples.translation: Buat dan visualisasikan quantum circuit dalam dua menit / Buat quantum circuit pertamamu dalam dua menit
examples.why: "under two minutes" is an upper bound; "dalam dua menit" reads as "in two minutes" and quietly drops the qualifier the marketing claim rests on. Occurs in both the description frontmatter and the lead sentence.

examples.source: so you can install whatever packages you wish ... without affecting the "base" Python environment on your machine. / if your Python environment becomes corrupted, you can easily delete it
examples.suggested: Pick one address form and hold it — e.g. "...tanpa memengaruhi lingkungan Python 'dasar' di mesin Anda" and "jika lingkungan Python Anda rusak, Anda bisa..."
examples.translation: jadi Anda bisa menginstal paket apa pun yang diinginkan ... tanpa memengaruhi lingkungan Python "dasar" di mesinmu. / jika lingkungan Python-mu rusak, Anda bisa dengan mudah menghapusnya
examples.why: Formal "Anda" and the informal clitic "-mu" collide inside the same sentence three times in this accordion; a native writer would never mix the two registers in one clause.

examples.source: two entangled qubits / a signature of quantum entanglement / all three of these qubits have been entangled
examples.suggested: Use one convention throughout — either "keterjeratan kuantum" alongside "saling terjerat", or keep "entanglement" in English in all three places.
examples.translation: dua qubit yang saling terjerat / tanda dari quantum entanglement / ketiga qubit ini telah saling terjerat
examples.why: The same concept is Indonesianized in sections 2 and 4 but left in English in section 3, so the learner sees no link between "saling terjerat" and "quantum entanglement" at the exact moment the result is being explained.

examples.source: However, you can use other Python distributions / navigate to your project directory / at the end of the circuit / to run a circuit on real quantum hardware
examples.suggested: Namun, Anda juga bisa... / masuk ke direktori proyek Anda / di akhir circuit / menjalankan circuit di hardware kuantum sungguhan
examples.translation: Tapi Anda bisa juga menggunakan distribusi Python lain / navigasi ke direktori proyekmu / di akhir Circuit / menjalankan Circuit di hardware quantum nyata
examples.why: "Tapi" is spoken register for documentation prose, "navigasi ke" is a direct calque of English "navigate to" (Indonesian uses "masuk ke"/"pindah ke"), and "Circuit" is left title-cased mid-sentence, which reads as heading capitalization leaking into body text.

examples.source: Follow the steps in the [Run your first circuit on hardware](/guides/hello-world) guide to run a circuit on real quantum hardware.
examples.suggested: Ikuti langkah-langkah di panduan [Jalankan circuit pertama Anda di hardware](/guides/hello-world) ...
examples.translation: Ikuti langkah-langkah di [Hello world](/guides/hello-world) untuk menjalankan Circuit di hardware quantum nyata.
examples.why: The descriptive link label was replaced by the bare page slug "Hello world", losing the signpost that tells the learner what the linked guide will have them do; the word "guide/panduan" is dropped as well.

editor_note: Semantically faithful throughout — no drift, no dropped caveats, and the subtle sentences land correctly ("less amenable to noise" → "meno soggetti al rumore", upstream/downstream → "circuito a monte / a valle", "acts trivially (as in I)" → "agisce in modo banale (come I)"). Terminology is correct and consistent (valore di aspettazione, sottocircuito, sotto-osservabile, autostato, base tomograficamente completa, base di Pauli; wire cutting / circuit cutting / circuit-knitting / hardware-efficient kept in English as the field does), and the informal "tu" holds ("consulta", "assicurati", "Se hai trovato"). Only two stylistic snags remain: the two section headings stack the preposition "su" three times ("Esempio su simulatore su piccola scala", "Esempio su hardware su larga scala"), which reads clumsy to a native ear, and "optiamo per una suddivisione uguale" is slightly unidiomatic for "we opt for equal partition" (Italian wants "in parti uguali"). Neither would mislead a learner.

examples.source: ## Small-scale simulator example  … ## Large-scale hardware example
examples.suggested: ## Esempio su piccola scala con simulatore … ## Esempio su larga scala su hardware
examples.translation: ## Esempio su simulatore su piccola scala … ## Esempio su hardware su larga scala
examples.why: Three-word headings that repeat the preposition "su" twice ("su simulatore su piccola scala") are clumsy in Italian; a native technical writer would break the chain by making the instrument a "con" phrase or reordering. Meaning is unaffected.

examples.source: For this tutorial, we opt for equal partition.
examples.suggested: Per questo tutorial, optiamo per una suddivisione in parti uguali.
examples.translation: Per questo tutorial, optiamo per una suddivisione uguale.
examples.why: "suddivisione uguale" is a calque of "equal partition"; Italian expresses this as "suddivisione in parti uguali" (or "partizione equa"). Understandable, but not what a native would write.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, no swapped quantities (the tricky "3 trillion+ executions" is correctly rendered "oltre 3.000 miliardi", "100+ physical qubits" and "30–35 qubit" are intact), and the informal "tu" register holds consistently ("dovresti", "Prenditi un momento", "Clicca sui triangoli"). The defects are surface-level: two untranslated capitalized English glossary leaks in running prose — "le azioni dei Gate quantistici" (should be "gate quantistici"/"porte quantistiche") and "rendono i Circuit molto complessi/profondi" (should be "i circuiti") — plus "quantum fluency" rendered as "fluidità quantistica" (fluidity, not fluency/padronanza) and "layers used to entangle many qubits" as "I livelli" (levels rather than layer/strati). A handful of English-syntax calques remain that a native technical writer would rewrite: "capitalizzare in anticipo sulle tecnologie", "Le organizzazioni che si tuffano ora", "il potere dei processori" (should be "la potenza"), and the ungrammatical "ancora a anni di distanza" (missing euphonic d; better "ancora lontani anni"). None of these would make a learner form a false belief — the concepts stay identifiable — so this is MINOR, not FAIL.

examples.source: The layers used to entangle many qubits make the circuits very complex / deep
examples.suggested: Gli strati (layer) usati per creare entanglement tra molti qubit rendono i circuiti molto complessi/profondi
examples.translation: I livelli usati per l'entanglement di molti qubit rendono i Circuit molto complessi/profondi
examples.why: Untranslated capitalized English glossary leak: "i Circuit" is a bare English plural mid-Italian-sentence where the natural, unambiguous term is "i circuiti". "livelli" (levels) is also the wrong sense of "layers" in a circuit-depth context — Italian usage is "strati"/"layer".

examples.source: Interactions between those states and actions of quantum gates can be carried out on all those states simultaneously.
examples.suggested: ... e le azioni dei gate quantistici ...
examples.translation: Le interazioni tra questi stati e le azioni dei Gate quantistici possono essere eseguite su tutti questi stati simultaneamente.
examples.why: "Gate" is capitalized mid-sentence as if it were a proper noun — a glossary-leak artifact. Italian keeps "gate" in English but lowercase (or uses "porte quantistiche"); the capital makes it read as an untranslated token rather than a domain term.

examples.source: Talent strategy and culture to build a high-performing team with quantum fluency.
examples.suggested: ... un team ad alte prestazioni con padronanza del quantum.
examples.translation: Strategia dei talenti e cultura aziendale per costruire un team ad alte prestazioni con fluidità quantistica.
examples.why: "fluidity" (fluidità) is not "fluency". The intended sense — people fluent in quantum concepts — is "padronanza"/"competenza"/"dimestichezza"; "fluidità quantistica" reads as a physical property, not a skill.

examples.source: While the risks are likely still years away, cybercriminals could be using "harvest now, decrypt later" schemes
examples.suggested: Sebbene i rischi siano probabilmente ancora lontani anni, i criminali informatici potrebbero già utilizzare schemi "harvest now, decrypt later"
examples.translation: Sebbene i rischi siano probabilmente ancora a anni di distanza, i criminali informatici potrebbero già utilizzare schemi "harvest now, decrypt later"
examples.why: "a anni di distanza" is a literal calque of "years away" and is also ungrammatical (missing euphonic d before the vowel). A native technical writer would write "ancora lontani anni" or "si concretizzeranno solo tra anni".

examples.source: capitalize early on yesterday's game-changing technologies ... Organizations that dive in now
examples.suggested: trarre vantaggio fin da subito dalle tecnologie rivoluzionarie di ieri ... Le organizzazioni che si muovono fin da ora
examples.translation: capitalizzare in anticipo sulle tecnologie rivoluzionarie di ieri ... Le organizzazioni che si tuffano ora
examples.why: Two English-syntax calques in adjacent paragraphs: "capitalizzare su" is an anglicism (Italian: "trarre vantaggio da", "sfruttare"), and "si tuffano" is a literal rendering of "dive in" that sounds colloquially odd in a business-strategy register.

examples.source: Our work with UC Berkeley demonstrates the power of currently available IBM Quantum processors
examples.suggested: ... dimostra la potenza dei processori IBM Quantum attualmente disponibili
examples.translation: Il nostro lavoro con UC Berkeley dimostra il potere dei processori IBM Quantum attualmente disponibili
examples.why: For hardware capability Italian uses "potenza", not "potere" (which denotes authority/influence). Recognizable but wrong register for a technical noun.

editor_note: The technical content is faithful throughout — I found no semantic drift: the constant/balanced (定数型/バランス型) definitions, the 1-vs-2 query comparison, the 2^n/2+1 worst case, the 1/2·(2^n/2−1)/(2^n−1) answer, the "exponential over deterministic, no significant speedup over probabilistic" contrast, the phase-kickback (位相キックバック) explanation and the BV promise s=00...00→constant all match the English exactly. What a native editor would fix is surface consistency and polish: "gate" is rendered three ways — 「次のGate」「$U_f$ Gate」「アダマールGate」 (lines 67/71/180) vs 「アダマールゲート」「NOTゲート」「$U_f$ ゲート」 (lines 582/594/600); "circuit diagram" becomes the hybrid 「Circuit図」 (lines 260/393/457) where 回路図 is standard, and line 457 uses 回路 and Circuit図 in adjacent sentences; and qubit alternates between "Qubit" and "qubit" within single sentences (line 216 「qubit 0からQubit nまで…qubit 0は常に最も右」, line 258 「qubit 0だけでなく両方のQubit」). One raw English word leaks untranslated — 「将来の量子コンピュータの exciting な可能性」 (line 725) — and there are two keigo slips (「ご覧いただくか」 line 39, 「得ていただけたことを願っています」 line 721) against the desu/masu-only convention, plus calques 「建設的に加算され」 for "add constructively" (line 632), 「トイ例」 for "toy example" (line 48) and the particle error 「出力を…アクセスできる」 (line 235, should be 出力にアクセス). コンピューター/コンピュータ also alternates (line 46 vs 721).

examples.source: the $U_f$ gate computes $f(x)$ … the Hadamard gate "H" … a Hadamard gate is applied to the $n$ input qubits, and a NOT gate plus a Hadamard
examples.suggested: Unify on katakana throughout: 「$U_f$ ゲート」「アダマールゲート『H』」「次のゲートを使って」
examples.translation: 「$U_f$ Gate」「アダマールGate『H』」 (lines 71, 180) vs 「アダマールゲート」「NOTゲート」「$U_f$ ゲート」 (lines 582, 594, 600)
examples.why: The same core term is split between an untranslated English 'Gate' and katakana ゲート within one file; a Japanese technical writer would never mix 「アダマールGate」 and 「アダマールゲート」 in the same document.

examples.source: Here's a circuit diagram of Deutsch's algorithm. … We can't peek into the box to look at the circuit diagram.
examples.suggested: 以下はDeutschのアルゴリズムの回路図です。… ボックスの中を覗いて回路図を見ることはできません。
examples.translation: 以下はDeutschのアルゴリズムのCircuit図です。… ボックスの中を覗いてCircuit図を見ることはできません。
examples.why: 「Circuit図」 is an English/Japanese hybrid that no Japanese source uses; 回路図 is the established term, and the file already uses 回路 for 'circuit' one sentence earlier at line 457, so this reads as an unedited splice.

examples.source: These results, collectively showed the exciting promise of future quantum computer
examples.suggested: これらの成果は総合して、将来の量子コンピューターが秘める大きな可能性を示し
examples.translation: これらの成果は総合して、将来の量子コンピュータの exciting な可能性を示し
examples.why: A raw English adjective is left untranslated mid-sentence — an obvious untranslated leak in an otherwise complete paragraph.

examples.source: Watch the module walkthrough by Dr. Katie McCormick below … We hope that … we've given you a better intuition
examples.suggested: …モジュールのウォークスルー動画を以下で見るか… / …より深い直感が得られたなら幸いです。
examples.translation: …モジュールのウォークスルー動画をご覧いただくか… / …より深い直感を得ていただけたことを願っています。
examples.why: 「ご覧いただく」/「いただけた」 are keigo, against this corpus's plain desu/masu convention for teaching material; the rest of the file is correctly plain, so these two stand out.

examples.source: If $s=0$, then the first two terms add constructively and the last two terms cancel
examples.suggested: $s=0$ の場合、最初の2項は強め合い、最後の2項は打ち消し合い
examples.translation: $s=0$ の場合、最初の2項は建設的に加算され、最後の2項は打ち消し合い
examples.why: 「建設的に加算され」 is a word-for-word calque of 'add constructively'; Japanese physics writing says 強め合う (paired naturally with the 打ち消し合う already used in the same sentence), so the calque breaks the constructive/destructive symmetry the sentence is teaching.

examples.source: the states of qubits 0 through n … so qubit 0 is always farthest right / he prepared a superposition state on *both* qubits, instead of only on qubit 0
examples.suggested: Pick one casing (e.g. 「Qubit 0」「Qubit n」) and apply it to all 24 occurrences.
examples.translation: qubit 0からQubit nまでの状態は…qubit 0は常に最も右に位置します / qubit 0だけでなく*両方の*Qubitに重ね合わせ状態を準備しました
examples.why: Qubit/qubit alternates inside single sentences, which looks like two merged translation passes; the concept stays identifiable but a native editor would normalize it.

editor_note: No misleading content: the protocol logic, the BB84 tables, the no-cloning argument (複製不可能定理), the 14%/23% mismatch discussions and all quiz items are faithful to the English. What a native editor would fix is terminology hygiene: "qubit" is rendered four different ways inside one file — 量子ビット (once, line 162), the English plural "Qubits" (10×, e.g. 「エンタングルしたQubitsを共有し」, 「そのQubitsに」, 「ランダムなQubitsをボブに送る」), "Qubit" as a counter (「約30Qubit以上」, 「127Qubitの」), and bare lowercase "qubit" (15×, all in the second half from line 463 on). "circuit" splits the same way: 13× "Circuit" (「問題を量子Circuit（回路）にマッピングする」, 「Circuit を引数としてサンプラーを使用して」) against 5× 回路 including the very next heading 「問題を量子回路にマッピングする」; "backend" likewise stays as "Backend" (line 391). An English plural -s glued onto a Japanese noun is something no Japanese technical writer produces. Two smaller items: line 162 invents a rationale the English does not make (「2つの固有状態を持つことを強調するためにQubitsと呼びます」 vs. the source's plain parenthetical "(emphasizing that qubits have two eigenstates)"), and line 39 breaks the no-keigo convention with 「ご覧いただくか…ご視聴ください」.

examples.source: Let's assume we are working with qubits ... the state-of-the-art quantum computers at IBM use qubits.
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering (量子ビット, or lowercase qubit) and use it everywhere; never the English plural "Qubits".
examples.translation: 量子ビット（…）を使って作業していると仮定しましょう。…IBM®の最先端の量子コンピューターはQubitsを使用しています。 / 「約30Qubit以上」「127Qubitの」 / 「同じ基底で準備・測定された qubit は決定論的な結果を持つため」
examples.why: Four renderings of the single most important term in one file (量子ビット / Qubits / Qubit / qubit), split roughly by section — prose sections use "Qubits", the post-processing sections use "qubit". The English plural -s attached to a Japanese noun (「そのQubitsに $|1\rangle$ を準備しなかった」, which is a single qubit) is a glossary keep-English leak, not a Japanese word.

examples.source: Step 1: Map your problem to a quantum circuit / Use the sampler to run your job, with the circuit as an argument.
examples.suggested: 量子回路 / 回路 throughout; also バックエンド or a single consistent form for "Backend" (line 391).
examples.translation: ステップ1：問題を量子Circuit（回路）にマッピングする … 「Circuit を引数としてサンプラーを使用してジョブを実行します。」
examples.why: The Qiskit-patterns list writes 量子Circuit（回路） and Circuit, while the immediately following heading writes 量子回路 — the same term glossed two ways within four lines. 回路 is the settled Japanese domain term; leaving "Circuit" capitalized mid-sentence reads as an untranslated placeholder.

examples.source: Let's assume we are working with qubits (emphasizing that qubits have two eigenstates).
examples.suggested: 量子ビット（2つの固有状態を持つ点を強調しておきます）を扱うものとしましょう。
examples.translation: 量子ビット（2つの固有状態を持つことを強調するためにQubitsと呼びます）を使って作業していると仮定しましょう。
examples.why: The English parenthetical simply reminds the reader of a fact; the Japanese turns it into a naming rationale — "we call them Qubits in order to emphasize that they have two eigenstates" — a claim the source never makes and which is not true of the name. Not misleading about the physics, but a fabricated justification.

examples.source: Watch the module walkthrough by Dr. Katie McCormick below, or click here to watch it on YouTube.
examples.suggested: 以下のDr. Katie McCormickによるモジュール解説動画を見るか、[こちら]からYouTubeで視聴してください。
examples.translation: 以下のDr. Katie McCormickによるモジュール解説動画をご覧いただくか、[こちら]からYouTubeでご視聴ください。
examples.why: ご覧いただく and ご視聴ください are exactly the keigo forms the file's convention excludes; the rest of the document holds plain desu/masu (…してください, …しましょう), so this opening line is out of register with everything after it.

examples.source: ### Check your understanding\n\nIf we really only care about English letters, how many bits do we need?
examples.suggested: Drop the added instruction, or keep it only where the English source carries the equivalent sentence.
examples.translation: ### 理解度の確認\n以下の問いを読み、答えを考えてから、三角形をクリックして解答を表示してください。
examples.why: An instruction sentence absent from this English file is injected before both 理解度の確認 accordions. It is harmless (the <details> widget does show a triangle) and matches boilerplate the English uses in other modules, but it is content added to a file whose source has none — worth normalizing rather than leaving locale-specific.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inversions, no swapped quantities, no dropped caveats; the stabilizer/bit-flip explanation, the ISA paragraph and the Step 4 conclusion ("비트 반전 코드가 많은 오류를 감지하고 정정하여 전체적으로 오류가 줄어든 것을 확인할 수 있습니다") all match the English. The defects are terminological: "circuit" and "qubit" are left as capitalized English words inside Korean sentences ("동적 양자 Circuit을 시연하고", "인코딩된 Qubit을", headings "비트 반전 스태빌라이저 Circuit 구축", "ISA Circuit 생성"), where every Korean quantum text writes 양자 회로 and 큐비트 — this reads as glossary leakage, not a native choice. It is also inconsistent within the file: line 60 uses lowercase "qubit" ("인코딩 qubit 중 어느 하나") while the rest uses "Qubit". Additionally the stabilizer sentence adds a gloss not in the English ("즉 파울리 연산자로 구성된"); it is technically correct and pedagogically helpful, but it is an insertion a strict editor would either drop or mark. Register is fine: standard 합니다체/해요체 mix, no 하십시오체 or 드리- humble forms.

examples.source: It demonstrates a dynamic quantum circuit that can protect an encoded qubit from a single bit-flip error, and then evaluates the bit-flip code performance.
examples.suggested: 인코딩된 큐비트를 단일 비트 반전 오류로부터 보호할 수 있는 동적 양자 회로를 시연하고, 비트 반전 코드의 성능을 평가합니다.
examples.translation: 인코딩된 Qubit을 단일 비트 반전 오류로부터 보호할 수 있는 동적 양자 Circuit을 시연하고, 비트 반전 코드의 성능을 평가합니다.
examples.why: '회로' and '큐비트' are the settled Korean renderings (양자 회로 / 큐비트). Leaving capitalized English 'Circuit'/'Qubit' inside Korean prose reads as untranslated glossary leakage; no Korean quantum engineer writes '동적 양자 Circuit'. Same pattern in the headings '비트 반전 스태빌라이저 Circuit 구축' and 'ISA Circuit 생성', and in '대상 시스템이 지원하는 ... Circuit과 옵저버블만 허용합니다'.

examples.source: It protects the state against a single bit-flip (X) error on any of the encoding qubits. ... The code requires five qubits
examples.suggested: 이 코드는 인코딩 큐비트 중 어느 하나에 대한 단일 비트 반전(X) 오류로부터 상태를 보호합니다. ... 이 코드에는 다섯 개의 큐비트가 필요합니다
examples.translation: 이 코드는 인코딩 qubit 중 어느 하나에 대한 단일 비트 반전(X) 오류로부터 상태를 보호합니다. ... 이 코드는 다섯 개의 Qubit이 필요합니다
examples.why: Within one paragraph the same term appears as lowercase 'qubit' and as capitalized 'Qubit' — an in-file inconsistency on the single most frequent domain term. '이 코드는 ... 필요합니다' is also a calqued subject-marking; '이 코드에는 ... 가 필요합니다' is the natural Korean.

examples.source: Stabilizer codes critically focus on correcting a discrete error set with support from the Pauli group $\Pi^n$.
examples.suggested: 스태빌라이저 코드는 파울리 군 $\Pi^n$에 서포트(support)를 갖는 이산 오류 집합을 정정하는 데 결정적으로 중점을 둡니다.
examples.translation: 스태빌라이저 코드는 파울리 군 $\Pi^n$에 서포트(support)를 갖는, 즉 파울리 연산자로 구성된 이산 오류 집합을 정정하는 데 주로 중점을 둡니다.
examples.why: The clause '즉 파울리 연산자로 구성된' is an inserted gloss with no counterpart in the English. It happens to be correct and helps the reader, so it does not mislead, but it is added content; 'critically' is also softened to '주로' (mainly) rather than the stronger 'crucially/결정적으로'.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the tricky precedence sentence ("옵션이 Primitive 초기화 중과 이후 모두에 지정된 경우, Primitive 초기화 이후에 설정된 값이 사용됩니다") and every compatibility-tab list match the English exactly, with no inverted conditions or dropped caveats, and the added gloss "회로 끝의 최종 측정" for "terminal measurements" is a genuine pedagogical improvement. Three editor-level nits: (1) "circuit" is split within the file — the glossary form "Circuit" is used everywhere ("동적 Circuit", "양자 Circuit") except lines 201 and 233, which switch to native "회로"; (2) `execution.init_qubits` renders "ground state" as "기저 상태" (line 153), which in a quantum-computing text reads ambiguously as "basis state" — "바닥 상태" is the unambiguous Korean for ground state; (3) "**기본값**: `backend.default_rep_delay`에 의해 지정됨" (line 165) is a stiff English passive calque. Register is uniform 합니다체 with no honorific/humble (드리-) forms — the standard Korean technical-doc register, consistently applied.

examples.source: Whether to reset the qubits to the ground state for each shot.
examples.suggested: 각 샷마다 Qubit을 바닥 상태로 리셋할지 여부.
examples.translation: 각 샷에 대해 Qubit을 기저 상태로 초기화할지 여부.
examples.why: 기저(基底) is the standard Korean word for *basis*, so "기저 상태" is routinely read as "basis state" in quantum-computing prose. The English specifically means the physical ground state; 바닥 상태 is the unambiguous term. Not misleading enough to teach a false concept (|0> is both), but a native technical editor would change it.

examples.source: Measurement twirling can only be applied to terminal measurements. / dynamic circuits
examples.suggested: 측정 트월링은 Circuit 끝의 최종 측정에만 적용할 수 있습니다.
examples.translation: 측정 트월링은 회로 끝의 최종 측정에만 적용할 수 있습니다. (vs. "동적 Circuit", "양자 Circuit" elsewhere)
examples.why: Within-file inconsistency: "circuit" is kept as the English glossary form "Circuit" in 9 places but rendered natively as "회로" in the two twirling notes. The concept stays identifiable, so MINOR — but the file should pick one rendering.

examples.source: **Default**: Given by `backend.default_rep_delay`
examples.suggested: **기본값**: `backend.default_rep_delay` 값
examples.translation: **기본값**: `backend.default_rep_delay`에 의해 지정됨
examples.why: "~에 의해 지정됨" is a direct calque of the English agentive passive; Korean technical writing normally drops the agent-marker here. Stiff rather than wrong.

editor_note: The Malay prose is genuinely fluent and every number, condition and claim checks out against the English (20 min runtime, 156Q Heron R2, 70% of aerodynamic theory, 13 = 12+1 parameters vs 3021/4701, loss 0.0015 after 28 lelaran, Step 315), so nothing here misleads a learner. The real defects are terminological: untranslated glossary leaks capitalized mid-sentence — "parameter Circuit awal", "12 parameter Circuit", "Setara dengan Circuit kami", "cara menentukan Backend" — where the file elsewhere translates freely and Malay would use "litar"; "dissipative systems" rendered "sistem penyebaran" (dispersion/spreading, not lesapan/dissipation, and confusingly distinct from the "resapan" already used for diffusion two lines earlier); "coupled PDEs" rendered "PDE bersepadu" ("integrated" rather than terganding); and "fluid" consistently rendered "cecair" (liquid) including in "Dinamik Cecair Berkomputer" for CFD, where standard Malay physics uses "bendalir" — awkward in a tutorial whose worked example is aerodynamic (gas) flow. A few stiff spots remain ("Menakjubkan," as a sentence adverb for "Surprisingly", "cara untuk plot keputusan", "Tolong luangkan masa" where "Sila" is the standard register) and the sentence-final period was dragged inside two link labels ("[kertas H-DES.]", "[borang untuk meminta akses.]").

examples.source: initial circuit parameters … 12 circuit parameters … The equivalent of our circuit … how to specify the backend
examples.suggested: parameter litar awal … 12 parameter litar … Setara dengan litar kami … cara menentukan backend
examples.translation: parameter Circuit awal … 12 parameter Circuit … Setara dengan Circuit kami … cara menentukan Backend
examples.why: English glossary leak, capitalized mid-sentence in four places, in a file that otherwise translates domain vocabulary; reads as an unmerged glossary artifact rather than a deliberate keep-English convention.

examples.source: describing phenomena occurring in fluid dynamics, gas dynamics, and nonlinear acoustics … by modeling dissipative systems
examples.suggested: …, antara lain, dengan memodelkan sistem lesapan (dissipative)
examples.translation: …, antara lain, dengan memodelkan sistem penyebaran
examples.why: "penyebaran" means spreading/dispersion, not dissipation — and it collides with "resapan" (diffusion) used one clause earlier for the convection–diffusion equation, blurring a distinction that matters for Burgers' equation.

examples.source: Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) … fluid dynamics … the fluid speed field … a flowing non-viscous fluid
examples.suggested: Dinamik Bendalir Berkomputer … dinamik bendalir … medan laju bendalir … bendalir tidak likat yang mengalir
examples.translation: Dinamik Cecair Berkomputer (CFD) … dinamik cecair … medan laju cecair … cecair tidak likat yang mengalir
examples.why: "cecair" is liquid; standard Malay for fluid is "bendalir". The tutorial's worked example is aerodynamic (gas) flow, and "dinamik cecair, dinamik gas" reads as a false liquid-vs-gas split where the English has fluid dynamics subsuming gas dynamics.

examples.source: solving non-linear multivariate coupled PDEs with classical tools remains challenging
examples.suggested: menyelesaikan PDE terganding berbilang pemboleh ubah tidak linear dengan alat klasik masih mencabar
examples.translation: menyelesaikan PDE bersepadu berbilang pemboleh ubah tidak linear dengan alat klasik masih mencabar
examples.why: "bersepadu" means integrated/unified; "coupled" (equations sharing unknowns) is "terganding/berganding" — and "bersepadu" risks being read as integration in a differential-equations context.

examples.source: Surprisingly, more than 70% of aerodynamic theory deals with inviscid flows.
examples.suggested: Yang menghairankan, lebih daripada 70% teori aerodinamik menangani aliran tidak likat.
examples.translation: Menakjubkan, lebih daripada 70% teori aerodinamik berkaitan dengan aliran tidak likat.
examples.why: Bare "Menakjubkan," as a sentence adverb is a direct calque of English "Surprisingly,"; a Malay technical writer would use "Yang menghairankan" / "Menariknya".

examples.source: plot a comparison to the PINN solution … demonstrates how to plot the result
examples.suggested: dan plotkan perbandingan dengan penyelesaian PINN … cara memplot keputusan tersebut
examples.translation: dan plot perbandingan dengan penyelesaian PINN … cara untuk plot keputusan tersebut
examples.why: "plot" is used as a bare English verb with no Malay affixation; "cara untuk plot" is not idiomatic Malay verb morphology.

examples.source: Please take a minute to provide feedback on this tutorial.
examples.suggested: Sila luangkan masa seminit untuk memberikan maklum balas tentang tutorial ini.
examples.translation: Tolong luangkan masa seminit untuk memberi maklum balas tentang tutorial ini.
examples.why: "Tolong" is a personal-favour imperative; documentation register uses "Sila". The rest of the file holds the standard "anda" convention correctly.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, no swapped numbers (156 qubit, 10 vs 50 percubaan, ~100 lelaran, AR=100% all match), and core renderings like "nisbah penghampiran", "keadaan asas", "penindasan ralat", "graf 3-sekata" and "sebutan counterdiabatic" are correct. What a native technical editor would change is terminology consistency: "circuit" is "litar" in the Overview/Description but is left as untranslated capitalized "Circuit" three times in the transpilation paragraphs ("kedalaman Circuit terbaik", "kerumitan Circuit tertentu", "sesetengah Circuit/masalah") — in the same sentence as "litar akhir"; and "entangling gates" is rendered two different ways ("get yang mengaitkan" then "get pengkaitan"), neither using the conventional belitan/keterjeratan family. "bias-field" becomes "medan berat sebelah" (which in Malay connotes unfairness/partiality rather than a physics bias term), saved only by the parenthetical gloss "(bias-field)" on first use. Finally, "instance" and "example" both collapse to "contoh", producing the circular "Contoh untuk menjalankan contoh ini boleh didapati dalam Contoh 3: Contoh penanda aras", plus a handful of English-syntax calques ("Berikut memberikan lebih butiran…", "boleh dikurangkan kepada", "dalam susunan kira-kira 100 lelaran"). None of these would teach a learner a false concept.

examples.source: …select the one that produces the best circuit depth… this depends heavily on the specific circuit structure and complexity. For some circuits/problems…
examples.suggested: …kedalaman litar terbaik… struktur dan kerumitan litar tertentu… untuk sesetengah litar/masalah…
examples.translation: …memilih yang menghasilkan kedalaman Circuit terbaik… ini sangat bergantung pada struktur dan kerumitan Circuit tertentu. Walau bagaimanapun, untuk sesetengah Circuit/masalah…
examples.why: 'litar' is used correctly everywhere else in the file (lines 30, 36, and even 'mengubah litar akhir' in this very sentence); leaving capitalized English 'Circuit' here is a glossary leak and an in-file split of the same term.

examples.source: …quantum circuits with shorter depth and fewer entangling gates. The circuits … use up to ten times fewer entangling gates than DQA…
examples.suggested: pick one form, e.g. 'get belitan' (or 'get keterjeratan') in both places
examples.translation: …litar kuantum dengan kedalaman yang lebih pendek dan bilangan get yang mengaitkan yang lebih sedikit. Litar algoritma bf-DCQO biasanya menggunakan … get pengkaitan berbanding DQA
examples.why: Two renderings of 'entangling gate' one sentence apart, and 'mengaitkan/pengkaitan' reads as 'linking/associating' rather than quantum entanglement, so the connection to belitan/keterjeratan is not obvious to a learner.

examples.source: The obtained distribution is used to calculate a so-called bias-field. The bias-field allows starting the next iteration…
examples.suggested: medan bias (bias-field) … Medan bias membolehkan…
examples.translation: Taburan yang diperoleh digunakan untuk mengira medan berat sebelah (bias-field). Medan berat sebelah membolehkan permulaan lelaran seterusnya…
examples.why: 'berat sebelah' in Malay means partial/unfair (a judgement about people), not a physics bias term; the gloss rescues the first mention but the bare repeat reads oddly to a technical reader.

examples.source: An example to run these instances can be found in Example 3: Benchmark instances.
examples.suggested: Contoh cara menjalankan kes penanda aras ini boleh didapati dalam Contoh 3: Kes penanda aras.
examples.translation: Contoh untuk menjalankan contoh ini boleh didapati dalam Contoh 3: Contoh penanda aras.
examples.why: 'instance' and 'example' are both flattened to 'contoh', so the sentence says 'an example to run these examples … in Example 3: Examples' — circular and harder to parse than the English.

examples.source: The following provides more details about the used algorithm… / solving an optimization problem on quantum hardware can be reduced to
examples.suggested: Bahagian berikut menerangkan dengan lebih lanjut… / …boleh diringkaskan kepada tiga langkah:
examples.translation: Berikut memberikan lebih butiran tentang algoritma yang digunakan… / menyelesaikan masalah pengoptimuman pada perkakasan kuantum boleh dikurangkan kepada:
examples.why: Both are word-order calques of the English; 'dikurangkan' carries the sense of reducing a quantity rather than 'reduced to a few steps', which is what the bullet list actually means.

examples.source: it also supports higher-order (HUBO) optimization problems / are NP-hard problems
examples.suggested: masalah pengoptimuman tertib lebih tinggi (HUBO) / masalah NP-sukar (or keep 'NP-hard')
examples.translation: ia juga menyokong masalah pengoptimuman peringkat tinggi (HUBO) / ialah masalah NP-susah
examples.why: 'peringkat tinggi' reads as 'high-level/advanced' rather than 'higher-order' in the polynomial sense, and 'NP-susah' uses the colloquial 'susah' where the established complexity-theory term is 'NP-sukar'; both remain recognizable from the acronyms but are not the conventional renderings.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, swapped quantities or dropped caveats — but a native technical editor would change several things. (1) "qubit" is rendered two incompatible ways in the same file: the Anglicised, mid-sentence-capitalised "Qubitów / Qubitu / Qubicie / Qubitach" (lines 29, 31, 36, 76, 138, 147, 161, 172) versus the correct Polish "kubit" inside the adjectives "czterokubitowego" (l.31) and "60-kubitowego" (l.323); "Backend/Backendu" is likewise capitalised mid-sentence (l.239, 241). (2) "observable" is rendered as the adjectival calque "obserwowalna" (standard Polish physics usage is "obserwabla"), and l.172 carries an outright case error — "obserwowalną zawsze działa trywialnie" should be nominative "obserwowalna zawsze działa"; "subobservable" becomes the clunky hyphenated "pod-obserwowalną" (l.198). (3) "uncut circuit" is split between "nieprzerwanego obwodu" (l.280, literally "uninterrupted") and "Nieprzycięty ... przycięty" (l.323, literally "trimmed"), neither being the natural "nieprzecięty/przecięty". (4) "upstream/downstream circuit" becomes "obwód wyżej/niżej w hierarchii" (l.229) — there is no hierarchy here, only position before/after the cut along the wire; "obwód przed cięciem / za cięciem" is what a Polish author would write. Informal "ty" register holds correctly ("Twój czas wykonania", "Jeśli ta praca wydała ci się interesująca").

examples.source: Since each subcircuit has fewer qubits and gates ... an example of wire cutting for a four-qubit GHZ state
examples.suggested: Ponieważ każdy podobwód ma mniej kubitów i bramek ... czterokubitowego stanu GHZ
examples.translation: Ponieważ każdy podobwód ma mniej Qubitów i bramek ... przykład cięcia przewodów dla czterokubitowego stanu GHZ
examples.why: The same concept appears as capitalised English-stem "Qubitów/Qubitu/Qubicie" in the running prose but as the correct Polish "kubit" inside compound adjectives. Mid-sentence capitalisation is ungrammatical in Polish, and the split makes the file look machine-glossed. Same problem with "Backendu" (l.241).

examples.source: Note the observable always acts trivially (as in $I$) on the extra qubit added for the virtual `Move` gate.
examples.suggested: Należy zauważyć, że obserwabla zawsze działa trywialnie (jako $I$) na dodatkowym kubicie dodanym dla wirtualnej bramki `Move`.
examples.translation: Należy zauważyć, że obserwowalną zawsze działa trywialnie (jako $I$) na dodatkowym Qubicie dodanym dla wirtualnej bramki `Move`.
examples.why: Two defects in one clause: the accusative "obserwowalną" is used where the sentence needs the nominative subject, and "obserwowalna" is an adjectival calque where Polish physics writing uses the noun "obserwabla". Meaning survives, but the sentence is ungrammatical.

examples.source: for each cut the upstream circuit must be measured in a Pauli basis, and the downstream circuit must be prepared in the eigenstate of the basis
examples.suggested: dla każdego cięcia obwód przed cięciem musi zostać zmierzony w bazie Pauliego, a obwód za cięciem musi zostać przygotowany w stanie własnym tej bazy
examples.translation: dla każdego cięcia obwód wyżej w hierarchii musi być zmierzony w bazie Pauliego, a obwód niżej w hierarchii musi być przygotowany w stanie własnym tej bazy
examples.why: "Upstream/downstream" here means position along the wire relative to the cut, not a hierarchical relation; "wyżej/niżej w hierarchii" imports a nesting metaphor the English does not have and blurs the temporal picture the tutorial is teaching.

examples.source: reconstruct the expectation value of the uncut circuit / The uncut, as well as the cut circuits, will be executed
examples.suggested: rekonstruujemy wartość oczekiwaną nieprzeciętego obwodu / Zarówno nieprzecięty, jak i przecięty obwód zostaną wykonane
examples.translation: rekonstruujemy wartość oczekiwaną nieprzerwanego obwodu / Nieprzycięty, jak i przycięty obwód, zostanie wykonany
examples.why: "uncut" is rendered inconsistently within one file, and neither variant is right: "nieprzerwany" means "uninterrupted/continuous" and "przycięty" means "trimmed". The article's own key operation is cięcie, so nieprzecięty/przecięty is the term that matches the rest of the page.

examples.source: Small-scale simulator example / Post-process and return result in desired classical format / Large-scale hardware example
examples.suggested: Przykład w małej skali na symulatorze / Przetwarzanie końcowe i zwrócenie wyniku w żądanym formacie klasycznym / Przykład w dużej skali na sprzęcie
examples.translation: Przykład małoskalowego symulatora / Post-przetwarzanie i zwracanie wyników w żądanym formacie klasycznym / Przykład wielkoskalowego sprzętu
examples.why: In both headings the size adjective attaches to the wrong noun — the Polish reads "example of a small-scale simulator" / "example of large-scale hardware" rather than "a small/large-scale example run on the simulator/hardware". "Post-przetwarzanie" (and "pod-eksperyment", l.258) are hyphenated calques where Polish uses "przetwarzanie końcowe" and the unhyphenated "podeksperyment".

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, no swapped quantities, all plan limits (10 minut / 28-dniowe okno kroczące, co najmniej 400 minut, 10 000 minut, 180 minut) and all "instead" recommendations survive intact, and the informal "ty" register holds without a single Pan/Pani slip. The one systematic defect is an untranslated glossary leak: "quantum circuits" is rendered "Circuit kwantowe" in all three plan sections ("Uruchamiaj swoje Circuit kwantowe...", lines 43, 64, 70) — the English head noun is left capitalized and in the singular under a Polish plural adjective, which no native writer would produce; the conventional term is "obwody kwantowe" (or "układy kwantowe"). Secondary: "fair-share scheduler" is rendered "harmonogram fair-share" (a schedule/timetable, not the scheduling component — "planista"/"mechanizm szeregowania fair-share" is right), "switch regions from the drop-down menu" is calqued as "zmieniać region z menu rozwijanego" (native: "za pomocą menu rozwijanego"), and "Kup z góry określoną liczbę minut" is structurally ambiguous between "pre-purchase a certain number" (intended) and "buy a predetermined number". None of these would give a learner a false belief about the plans.

examples.source: Run your quantum circuits on the world's best QPUs for free
examples.suggested: Uruchamiaj swoje obwody kwantowe na najlepszych QPU na świecie bezpłatnie
examples.translation: Uruchamiaj swoje Circuit kwantowe na najlepszych QPU na świecie bezpłatnie
examples.why: Glossary leak: the core domain term "circuit" is left in English, capitalized and morphologically inert (singular "Circuit" carrying the plural adjective "kwantowe"). Repeated identically in the Open, Pay-As-You-Go and Premium sections. Polish docs use "obwody kwantowe"; the learner still recognizes the concept, so this is imperfect-but-recognizable, not misleading.

examples.source: Learn about the [fair-share scheduler](/guides/fair-share-scheduler)
examples.suggested: Poznaj [mechanizm szeregowania fair-share](/guides/fair-share-scheduler)
examples.translation: Poznaj [harmonogram fair-share](/guides/fair-share-scheduler)
examples.why: "Harmonogram" is a schedule/timetable — a document — whereas a scheduler is the queueing component that assigns QPU time. The link label promises a timetable rather than a scheduling mechanism, flattening what the target page actually teaches.

examples.source: you can switch regions from the drop-down menu at the top of the Platform dashboard
examples.suggested: region możesz zmienić za pomocą menu rozwijanego u góry pulpitu platformy
examples.translation: możesz zmieniać region z menu rozwijanego u góry pulpitu platformy
examples.why: Direct calque of English "from the drop-down menu": Polish uses instrumental "za pomocą / w menu rozwijanym" for operating a control; "z menu" reads as extracting something out of the menu. Grammatical but audibly translated.

examples.source: Pre-purchase a certain number of minutes (at least 400) for running quantum jobs
examples.suggested: Wykup z góry pewną liczbę minut (co najmniej 400) na uruchamianie zadań kwantowych
examples.translation: Kup z góry określoną liczbę minut (co najmniej 400) na uruchamianie zadań kwantowych
examples.why: "z góry określoną liczbę" parses most naturally as "a predetermined number of minutes" (an amount fixed by IBM) rather than "pre-purchase a certain number" (an amount the user chooses). Moving the prefix onto the verb ("Wykup z góry pewną liczbę") removes the ambiguity.

examples.source: This service is recommended for those who are exploring ... and need high control over their resources and data.
examples.suggested: ... dla osób badających klasyczne algorytmy i aplikacje kwantowe oraz potrzebujących wysokiego stopnia kontroli nad zasobami i danymi.
examples.translation: Ta usługa jest zalecana dla osób badających klasyczne algorytmy i aplikacje kwantowe, które potrzebują wysokiego stopnia kontroli nad swoimi zasobami i danymi.
examples.why: The relative pronoun "które" can attach to "aplikacje kwantowe" as readily as to "osób", so the sentence momentarily reads as "applications that need high control". A participial "potrzebujących" binds the clause unambiguously to the people, as the English does.

editor_note: Nothing in this file misleads: the physics is faithful (mixed state at the cut, tomographically complete Pauli basis, upstream measured / downstream prepared in the eigenstate, +1 ideal value, "aumentará em 1" for the extra qubit) and the core terms are right and consistent — "valor esperado", "observável"/"subobservável", "corte de fios", "primitiva Sampler", "transpilamos", "backend", "autoestado". The editorial defects are: (1) "gate" is rendered two ways within the file — "portas" in the Background prose (l.29 "menos portas ou qubits", l.36 "menos qubits e portas") but "gate/gates" everywhere in the body (l.161/172 "gate virtual `Move`", l.241 "conjunto de gates base"); (2) l.323 "Os circuitos não cortado e cortado" is an agreement mismatch (plural noun, singular adjectives) that no native technical writer would leave; (3) "site de qubit" (l.76) is a calque of "qubit site" where PT physics uses "sítio"; (4) "Esta técnica está acessível no addon" (l.29) is a literal rendering of "is accessible in" where "está disponível" is the natural PT. Informal "você" convention holds ("Se você achou este trabalho interessante", l.429).

examples.source: …subcircuits involving fewer gates or qubits… / the basis gate set of the backend
examples.suggested: Pick one convention for the whole file — either "porta" throughout ("porta virtual `Move`", "conjunto de portas base") or "gate" throughout ("menos gates ou qubits").
examples.translation: …subcircuitos menores envolvendo menos portas ou qubits… / o conjunto de gates base do backend
examples.why: The same domain term is split between "porta" (Background only) and "gate" (entire body). Both are defensible in pt-BR on their own, but mixing them inside one tutorial makes the reader wonder whether "porta" and "gate" denote different things. Concept stays identifiable, so MINOR.

examples.source: The uncut, as well as the cut circuits, will be executed on IBM Quantum® hardware:
examples.suggested: Tanto o circuito não cortado quanto o cortado serão executados em hardware IBM Quantum®:
examples.translation: Os circuitos não cortado e cortado serão executados em hardware IBM Quantum®:
examples.why: "Os circuitos não cortado e cortado" pairs a plural noun with two singular adjectives — ungrammatical and visibly machine-shaped. The meaning survives (both circuits run on hardware), so it is stiffness, not drift.

examples.source: …is +1 for every qubit site i irrespective of the values of φ⃗
examples.suggested: …é $+1$ para cada sítio de qubit $i$…
examples.translation: …é $+1$ para cada site de qubit $i$ independentemente dos valores de $\vec{\phi}$
examples.why: "site" is left as the English word; Portuguese condensed-matter/MBL literature uses "sítio" (sítio da rede). "site" additionally collides with the everyday PT meaning of website. Recognizable in context, hence MINOR.

examples.source: This technique is accessible in the Circuit cutting Qiskit addon
examples.suggested: Esta técnica está disponível no addon Qiskit de corte de circuito
examples.translation: Esta técnica está acessível no addon Qiskit de corte de circuito
examples.why: "está acessível" is a word-for-word carry-over of "is accessible"; in PT technical prose a feature shipped in a package "está disponível em". Pure translationese, no meaning change.

editor_note: The mathematical argument is faithful throughout (no-cloning proof, the |γ0⟩/|δ1⟩ inner-product argument, and the orthogonality conclusion all track the English exactly), and the informal "você" register holds ("alguém te entrega um sistema", "tudo que você tem em mãos"). What a native editor would fix is a cluster of untranslated/inconsistent terminology in the third section: "circuito" is left in English and capitalized three times — "a Circuits quânticos que consistem em…", "usados pelo Circuit de qualquer forma", "em Circuits quânticos como este" — while the very same paragraphs correctly say "circuito quântico"; likewise "gate" leaks once as "um Gate NOT controlado" (line 177) against "uma operação NOT controlada" five lines earlier. Compounding this, "porta" (feminine) is given masculine agreement twice: "qualquer número de portas unitários" (192) and "todos os portas unitários" (198) — it should be "portas unitárias" / "todas as portas unitárias". There is also a straight typo, "Raciocínando" for "Raciocinando" (237), and a small connective drift where "For example, we can clone a qubit standard basis state" becomes "De fato, podemos clonar…" (172), turning an example into an assertion of fact right after the preceding sentence already used "por exemplo". None of these mislead a learner; the concepts stay identifiable and the physics is intact.

examples.source: We'll restrict our attention to quantum circuits that consist of any number of unitary gates … these qubits can be used by the circuit in any way that might be beneficial. It is very common to make use of workspace qubits in quantum circuits like this.
examples.suggested: … a circuitos quânticos que consistem em qualquer número de portas unitárias … podem ser usados pelo circuito de qualquer forma que seja benéfica … em circuitos quânticos como este.
examples.translation: Vamos restringir nossa atenção a Circuits quânticos que consistem em qualquer número de portas unitários … esses qubits podem ser usados pelo Circuit de qualquer forma que seja benéfica. É muito comum fazer uso de qubits de espaço de trabalho em Circuits quânticos como este.
examples.why: Untranslated, capitalized English "Circuits"/"Circuit" glossary leak, inconsistent with "circuito quântico" used correctly in the same passage (lines 193, 194, 205, 222).

examples.source: This approach of using a controlled-NOT gate would not succeed in creating a clone of the state |+⟩, for instance.
examples.suggested: Essa abordagem, usando uma porta NOT controlada, não teria sucesso em criar um clone do estado |+⟩, por exemplo.
examples.translation: Essa abordagem usando um Gate NOT controlado não teria sucesso em criar um clone do estado $\vert + \rangle,$ por exemplo.
examples.why: English "Gate" left untranslated and capitalized, inconsistent with "uma operação NOT controlada" used five lines earlier for the same object; elsewhere the file uses "portas" for gates.

examples.source: any number of unitary gates … the combined action of all of the unitary gates in our circuit
examples.suggested: qualquer número de portas unitárias … a ação combinada de todas as portas unitárias em nosso circuito
examples.translation: qualquer número de portas unitários … a ação combinada de todos os portas unitários em nosso circuito
examples.why: Gender-agreement error: "porta" is feminine in Portuguese, so "os portas unitários" is ungrammatical and immediately marks the text as machine output to a native reader.

examples.source: Reasoning similarly for |φ⟩ in place of |ψ⟩, we conclude that
examples.suggested: Raciocinando de forma análoga para |φ⟩ no lugar de |ψ⟩, concluímos que
examples.translation: Raciocínando de forma análoga para $\vert\phi\rangle$ no lugar de $\vert\psi\rangle,$ concluímos que
examples.why: Misspelling: "Raciocínando" carries a spurious accent; the correct gerund is "Raciocinando".

examples.source: For example, we can clone a qubit standard basis state using a controlled-NOT operation:
examples.suggested: Por exemplo, podemos clonar um estado de qubit da base padrão usando uma operação NOT controlada:
examples.translation: De fato, podemos clonar um estado de qubit da base padrão usando uma operação NOT controlada:
examples.why: "For example" (an illustration of the preceding claim) is upgraded to "De fato" ("indeed/in fact"), an assertion; the English's example-chain structure with the prior sentence's "por exemplo" is lost. Minor, non-misleading.

editor_note: Nothing here misleads a learner — the physics, the four-step pattern and the numbers are all faithful, and the informal "tu" holds throughout ("post-procesezi", "înlocuiește pur și simplu", "Consultă", "Ține minte"). The dominant defect is a glossary capitalization leak: common nouns are capitalized mid-sentence ("cu ``36`` de Qubiți", "Transpilează ansatz-ul pentru Backend", "vom optimiza Circuitul nostru", "cu mai puține Gate-uri", "pase de Transpiler Qiskit") — never Romanian orthography — and it is applied inconsistently, since the same words appear lowercase elsewhere ("circuit cuantic" l.14, "După optimizarea circuitului" l.202). "Samples" is also split within the file: "eșantioane" in the intro and Steps 1–2 versus "mostre" in Step 3 and the results paragraph ("colectăm mostre", "mostrele cuantice din această demonstrație"). Smaller items: the restrictive "only" is dropped from "produce samples of the members of S only"; the hedge in "SQD is known to work well" is flattened to a flat "SQD funcționează bine"; the calque "funcția de undă este susținută într-un set de stări de bază" for mathematical "supported" (native: "are suport în"); a typo "operatorii fermonici" (→ "fermionici"); and a relative-pronoun agreement error, "un set de stări de bază ale cărei dimensiuni" (→ "a cărui dimensiune").

examples.source: a ``36``-qubit quantum circuit ansatz / Transpile the ansatz for the backend / fewer gates / Qiskit transpiler passes
examples.suggested: …cu ``36`` de qubiți / …pentru backend / mai puține porți (gate-uri) / pase de transpiler Qiskit
examples.translation: un ansatz de circuit cuantic cu ``36`` de Qubiți / Transpilează ansatz-ul pentru Backend / mai puține Gate-uri / pase de Transpiler Qiskit
examples.why: Glossary-driven capitalization leaks into running prose. Romanian does not capitalize common nouns mid-sentence, and the file itself is inconsistent about it ('circuit cuantic' lowercase at l.14 and 'După optimizarea circuitului' at l.202 vs 'Circuitul nostru' at l.160).

examples.source: samples / collect samples / random samples / the quantum samples in this demo
examples.suggested: eșantioane throughout ('colectăm eșantioane', 'eșantioane aleatoare', 'eșantioanele cuantice')
examples.translation: eșantioane / colectăm mostre / mostre aleatoare / mostrele cuantice din această demonstrație
examples.why: The core term 'samples' is rendered two ways inside one file. 'eșantioane' is used in the intro and Steps 1–2 and matches the surrounding derived forms ('eșantionare', 'eșantionat', 'subeșantioane'), so the switch to 'mostre' in Steps 3–4 breaks the chain a reader is following.

examples.source: The role of the quantum device is to produce samples of the members of $\mathcal{S}$ only.
examples.suggested: Rolul dispozitivului cuantic este de a produce eșantioane doar ale membrilor din $\mathcal{S}$.
examples.translation: Rolul dispozitivului cuantic este de a produce eșantioane ale membrilor din $\mathcal{S}$.
examples.why: The restrictive 'only' is dropped. The remaining sentence is still true, so it does not mislead, but the pedagogical point — that the device is needed for nothing more than sampling inside S — is lost.

examples.source: SQD is known to work well when the target eigenstate is sparse: the wave function is supported in a set of basis states $\mathcal{S}$ whose size does not increase exponentially…
examples.suggested: Se știe că SQD funcționează bine atunci când starea proprie țintă este rară: funcția de undă are suport într-un set de stări de bază $\mathcal{S}$ a cărui dimensiune nu crește exponențial…
examples.translation: SQD funcționează bine atunci când starea proprie țintă este rară: funcția de undă este susținută într-un set de stări de bază $\mathcal{S}$ ale cărei dimensiuni nu cresc exponențial…
examples.why: Three things in one sentence: the hedge 'is known to' is flattened to a bare assertion; 'is supported' is calqued as 'este susținută', which in Romanian reads as 'is backed/upheld' rather than the mathematical notion of support; and 'ale cărei dimensiuni' does not agree with the masculine/neuter antecedent 'un set' (→ 'a cărui dimensiune').

examples.source: …where each line take a zig-zag shape due the heavy-hex connectivity of the target hardware.
examples.suggested: …unde fiecare linie capătă o formă de zig-zag datorită conectivității heavy-hex a hardware-ului țintă.
examples.translation: …unde fiecare linie ia o formă zig-zag din cauza conectivității heavy-hex a hardware-ului țintă.
examples.why: 'ia o formă' is a word-for-word carry-over of English 'take a shape'; a Romanian technical writer would use 'capătă/are o formă'. 'din cauza' also carries a negative connotation here, where the zig-zag is a deliberate design consequence ('datorită').

examples.source: are the fermionic creation/annihalation operators
examples.suggested: sunt operatorii fermionici de creare/anihilare
examples.translation: sunt operatorii fermonici de creare/anihilare
examples.why: Simple misspelling of the domain adjective: 'fermonici' → 'fermionici'. Recognizable, but it is the key term of the Hamiltonian paragraph.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — every quantity, condition and caveat survives intact (7 felii / 6 din cele 8 grupuri, "depășește 8", "5e-3 eroare/felie * 10 felii = 5e-2", the L1-norm and p_norm caveats), and the informal "tu" register holds (Reține, consultă, vei vedea, să imporți). What a native editor would change is surface: a mangled participle "experimentele backpropagateate" (Step 3), a mis-parsed "un Estimator primitiv" for "the ``Estimator`` primitive" — in Romanian "primitiv" reads as the adjective "rudimentary", the correct rendering is "primitiva ``Estimator``" — and glossary-substitution artifacts that capitalize common nouns mid-sentence and break the plural: "un Circuit cuantic", "mai puține Circuit-uri cuantice de executat" (native: "circuite cuantice"), "Qubiții", "Gate-urile", "Backend". The same term also splits within the file: "Circuit" capitalized in the intro and Step 2 bullet list but lowercase "circuitul" everywhere else. Two further calques: "indicii ... sunt bazați pe zero" (native: "indexați de la zero") and "să pasezi instanța de Backend în constructor" (native: "să transmiți/să treci"). None of this would mislead a learner about operator backpropagation.

examples.source: Finally, we can run the backpropagated experiments and compare them with the full experiment
examples.suggested: În final, putem rula experimentele backpropagate și le putem compara cu experimentul complet
examples.translation: În final, putem rula experimentele backpropagateate și le putem compara cu experimentul complet
examples.why: "backpropagateate" is not a word in any language — the English participle "backpropagated" has had a Romanian participial ending glued onto it. Elsewhere the file correctly writes "valoarea de așteptare backpropagată" and "am backpropagat 7 felii", so this is an isolated malformation.

examples.source: We use a statevector-based ``Estimator`` primitive to illustrate the effect of truncation on the output.
examples.suggested: Folosim primitiva ``Estimator`` bazată pe statevector pentru a ilustra efectul trunchierii asupra rezultatului.
examples.translation: Folosim un Estimator primitiv bazat pe statevector pentru a ilustra efectul trunchierii asupra rezultatului.
examples.why: In Qiskit "primitive" is a noun naming a class of objects (Sampler/Estimator). Rendering it as the adjective "primitiv" makes the Romanian read "a rudimentary Estimator", which is not what the English says and detaches the sentence from the Qiskit primitives vocabulary the learner needs.

examples.source: Truncating terms can result in fewer quantum circuits to execute
examples.suggested: Trunchierea termenilor poate duce la mai puține circuite cuantice de executat
examples.translation: Trunchierea termenilor poate duce la mai puține Circuit-uri cuantice de executat
examples.why: Glossary-substitution artifact: the common noun is capitalized mid-sentence and given an English-style hyphenated plural. Romanian pluralizes natively as "circuite". The same file writes lowercase "circuitul"/"circuite" elsewhere, so the term is split within the file (also affects "un Circuit cuantic", "într-un singur Circuit", "Qubiții", "Gate-urile", "Backend").

examples.source: Note, that the indices of this new `reduced_coupling_map` are again zero-based.
examples.suggested: Notă: indicii acestui nou `reduced_coupling_map` sunt din nou indexați de la zero.
examples.translation: Notă: indicii acestui nou `reduced_coupling_map` sunt din nou bazați pe zero.
examples.why: "bazați pe zero" is a word-for-word calque of "zero-based" that a Romanian technical writer would not produce; the established phrasing is "indexați de la zero" / "numerotați de la zero".

examples.source: one would import the EstimatorV2 from ``qiskit-ibm-runtime`` and pass the backend instance into the constructor
examples.suggested: ar trebui să imporți [EstimatorV2] din ``qiskit-ibm-runtime`` și să transmiți instanța de backend constructorului
examples.translation: ar trebui să imporți [EstimatorV2] din ``qiskit-ibm-runtime`` și să pasezi instanța de Backend în constructor
examples.why: "a pasa" is a sports borrowing in Romanian, not the verb used for passing an argument; "a transmite" / "a trece" is standard. The preceding clause "pe Backend-ul pe care experimentele au fost transpilate" also drops the required preposition ("pentru care" / "către care").

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, dropped caveats or swapped quantities — and the informal register (تحتاج، حسابك، استدعِ، جرِّب) holds consistently, but a native technical editor would change several things. "gate-folding ZNE" is rendered "تدوير البوابات ZNE" (line 17), i.e. *gate twirling*, colliding with "تدوير Pauli" two words earlier and naming the wrong mechanism for ZNE noise amplification (should be طي البوابات). "observable" is rendered "مراقب/المراقبات" (lines 15, 81, 83, 99, 126) — readable as مُراقَب and consistent, but the conventional Arabic domain term is المؤثر القابل للرصد / الكمية المرصودة, and "مراقب" invites the observer/observable confusion that is especially costly in a quantum text. "circuit" is split within one sentence between the English "الـ Circuits" and Arabic "الدائرة" (line 126), and twice appears as the broken definite form "الـ دائرة" (lines 99, 126) where the glossary prefix was pasted onto an already-Arabic noun. Smaller: "instruction set architecture" is inverted to "مجموعة تعليمات المعمارية" (line 99, should be معمارية مجموعة التعليمات), "Open Plan" is over-translated to "الخطة المجانية" instead of the product name الخطة المفتوحة (line 116), and "كيفية الـ Transpile محليًا" (line 161) is a stiff calque.

examples.source: including dynamical decoupling, Pauli-twirling, gate-folding ZNE, PEA, and PEC
examples.suggested: بما فيها الفصل الديناميكي، وتدوير Pauli (twirling)، وZNE بطي البوابات (gate folding)، وPEA، وPEC
examples.translation: بما فيها الفصل الديناميكي، وتدوير Pauli، وتدوير البوابات ZNE، وPEA، وPEC
examples.why: "gate-folding" becomes "تدوير البوابات" (gate twirling/rotating), reusing the very word just used for Pauli-twirling. The reader is told ZNE amplifies noise by twirling gates rather than by folding them, so a named technique is described by the wrong mechanism.

examples.source: computes the expectation values for one or more observables … 2. Create a circuit and an observable
examples.suggested: يحسب … قيم التوقع لمؤثر قابل للرصد (observable) واحد أو أكثر … ‏2. إنشاء دائرة ومؤثر قابل للرصد
examples.translation: يحسب … قيم التوقع لمراقب واحد أو أكثر … ‏2. إنشاء دائرة ومراقب
examples.why: "مراقب" is the active participle "observer/monitor"; in a quantum text this is exactly the word a learner must NOT attach to an observable operator. It is used consistently and is recoverable from the surrounding code, so it is imperfect rather than misleading — but المؤثر القابل للرصد / الكمية المرصودة is the conventional rendering.

examples.source: The circuit and observable need to be transformed … The circuit, observable, and optional parameter value sets are input as …
examples.suggested: يجب تحويل الدائرة والمرصودة … تُدخَل الدائرة والمرصودة ومجموعات قيم المعاملات الاختيارية
examples.translation: يجب تحويل الـ دائرة والمراقب … تُدخَل الـ دائرة والمراقب ومجموعات قيم المعاملات الاختيارية
examples.why: "الـ دائرة" is not Arabic: the keep-English article prefix "الـ" has been glued onto an already-definite Arabic noun, leaving a stray dangling ـ. A native writer would simply write الدائرة.

examples.source: expectation values for the input circuits and observables
examples.suggested: قيم التوقع للدوائر والمرصودات المُدخَلة. تُدخَل الدائرة والمرصودة …
examples.translation: قيم التوقع للـ Circuits والمراقبات المُدخَلة. تُدخَل الـ دائرة والمراقب …
examples.why: "circuit" is rendered as the English "Circuits" and as Arabic "دائرة" in the same two-sentence passage (and the file switches between them from §2 onward). Both are defensible conventions; mixing them inside one paragraph is not.

examples.source: referred to as *instruction set architecture (ISA)* circuits
examples.suggested: المُشار إليها بدوائر *معمارية مجموعة التعليمات (ISA)*
examples.translation: المُشار إليها بـ *دوائر مجموعة تعليمات المعمارية (ISA)*
examples.why: The genitive chain is inverted: as written it reads "the architecture's instruction set" rather than "instruction set architecture". The ISA acronym rescues it, so the concept stays identifiable, but the Arabic phrase names the wrong head noun.

examples.source: Note that Open Plan users cannot submit session jobs.
examples.suggested: لاحظ أن مستخدمي الخطة المفتوحة (Open Plan) لا يمكنهم إرسال مهام الجلسات.
examples.translation: لاحظ أن مستخدمي الخطة المجانية لا يمكنهم إرسال مهام جلسات.
examples.why: "Open Plan" is an IBM Quantum product name; rendering it as "الخطة المجانية" (the free plan) substitutes a description for the name the learner must look for in the console, even though the description happens to be accurate today.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, no swapped quantities (30 لقطة vs 170,000 لقطة, 99% عتبة الثقة, 10,000 لقطة لكل دائرة all correct), and the key conceptual contrast is handled well: error suppression = كبت الأخطاء vs error mitigation = تخفيف الأخطاء is kept distinct and consistent, as are قبيت / لقطات (shots). Register is correctly informal singular throughout (حدِّد، شغِّل، استرجع، يمكنك) with no antum slips. What a native technical editor would change: (1) "observable" is rendered مراقِب ("observer", an agent noun) in زوج دائرة-مراقِب and أنشئ مؤثر هيرميتي عشوائيًا ومراقِبًا — consistent but the wrong part of speech; the field uses مؤثر قابل للرصد / الكمية المرصودة, especially jarring beside the correct مؤثرات for "operators" two lines earlier; (2) "invariant to global shifts and scaling" becomes لا يتأثر بالإزاحات الكلية والقياس, where القياس reads as "measurement", not "scaling" (التحجيم / تغيير المقياس) — the following sentence about زيادة انتشارها rescues the intuition, so it does not mislead outright; (3) three within-file inconsistencies: "primitive" is بدائية at ## بدائية Estimator but the parallel heading is left raw as ## Sampler primitive (and استخدم Sampler primitive in the body); "function" is دالة everywhere except الوظيفة in the backend-support admonition, where وظيفة also does double duty for "job" in معرّف الوظيفة in the changelog; and "variational" is المتغيرة in the arXiv list but المتغيري in محلل القيم الذاتية المتغيري الكمومي. (4) "benchmarking" is rendered with the coined noun معيارية (معيارية الخوارزميات المنشورة، عمليات المعيارية السابقة), which no Arabic technical writer would use for benchmark runs — قياس الأداء المرجعي / اختبارات الأداء is the convention.

examples.source: determine the expectation value of a single circuit-observable pair … generate a random Hermitian operator and an observable
examples.suggested: زوج دائرة–مؤثر قابل للرصد … أنشئ مؤثرًا هيرميتيًا عشوائيًا ومؤثرًا قابلًا للرصد (أو: كمية مرصودة)
examples.translation: لتحديد قيمة التوقع لزوج دائرة-مراقِب واحد … أنشئ مؤثر هيرميتي عشوائيًا ومراقِبًا
examples.why: مراقِب is the agent noun 'observer', not the quantum-mechanical observable (a Hermitian operator). It is at least used consistently, and the surrounding code (SparsePauliOp) keeps the concept identifiable, so it does not teach a false concept — but it is the wrong conventional term and sits oddly next to the correct مؤثر used for 'operators' in the same sentence.

examples.source: This metric is used because it is invariant to global shifts and scaling in the range of attainable values.
